goal: Turn stable Phase 56Y identities into compatible repeat-measurement, accepted-operation, delivered-input, and explicit hold panels.
publication_rule: Publish only when the entity, universe, stage, observation period, unit, method, and denominator are compatible; otherwise retain an explicit In Review hold.
authority_rule: Two points are not automatically a durable trend, agency reporting is not independent validation, and construction, accepted operation, output, outcome, closeout, implementation, and closure remain distinct.

records.title: DOT IIJA aggregate: obligation and outlay shares rise across a changing authority denominator
records.finding: From March 31, 2025 to May 31, 2026, reported DOT IIJA obligations rose from $272.869 billion to $392.472 billion and outlays from $143.257 billion to $237.220 billion; the obligated share moved from 67.30 to 71.92 percent and the outlay share from 35.33 to 43.47 percent.
records.denominator: Two DOT-wide formula-plus-discretionary IIJA financial statements; adjusted authority changed from $405.476 billion to $545.692 billion between observations.
evidence_limits: The denominator increased by about $140.216 billion, so percentage-point movement is not a fixed-cohort completion rate.
Obligations and outlays are lifecycle measures, not accepted assets or outcomes.
Two observations do not establish a durable trend or causal explanation.
records.next_action: Add later statements under the same accounting method and separate stable program cohorts that reach accepted delivery, service, use, and outcomes.
records.authority_boundary: Selection, agreement, obligation, payment, construction, delivery, acceptance, operation, output, realized outcome, closeout, implementation, and closure remain separate. Repeated agency reporting does not establish independent causal attribution or a cross-entity ranking.

records.title: FHWA IIJA: outlays rise from 49.3 to 55.4 percent while authority expands
records.finding: FHWA obligations rose from $180.678 billion to $262.910 billion and outlays from $112.370 billion to $177.778 billion between the two DOT statements; obligation share rose 2.7 points and outlay share rose 6.1 points.
records.denominator: FHWA formula-plus-discretionary IIJA funding; adjusted authority changed from $227.871 billion to $320.662 billion.
evidence_limits: The formula-plus-discretionary denominator changed materially.
Payments do not establish completion, acceptance, road condition, safety, travel-time, or emissions outcomes.
The panel does not support comparison with FTA or FRA performance.
records.next_action: Track a stable FHWA program cohort into accepted projects, service condition, safety, and use measures.

records.title: FTA IIJA: obligation and outlay shares rise under a larger adjusted-authority base
records.finding: FTA obligations rose from $37.280 billion to $56.710 billion and outlays from $18.595 billion to $34.573 billion; the obligation share moved from 48.2 to 57.3 percent and the outlay share from 24.0 to 34.9 percent.
records.denominator: FTA formula-plus-discretionary IIJA funding; adjusted authority changed from $77.356 billion to $98.931 billion.
evidence_limits: The authority base is not fixed.
An outlay is a payment, not an accepted transit asset or operating result.
The panel does not establish ridership, reliability, accessibility, safety, or emissions outcomes.

records.title: FRA IIJA: dollars obligated rise while the obligation share falls under a larger denominator
records.finding: FRA obligations rose from $35.476 billion to $41.516 billion and outlays from $2.589 billion to $7.279 billion, but the obligation share moved from 67.2 to 63.0 percent as adjusted authority rose from $52.795 billion to $65.856 billion.
records.denominator: FRA formula-plus-discretionary IIJA funding across two DOT statements with a changing authority base.
evidence_limits: The 4.2-point obligation-share decline is a denominator effect and is not evidence that obligations were reversed.
The 6.2-point outlay-share increase remains a payment measure.
No project completion, service, capacity, safety, or passenger outcome is established.

records.title: Hanford DFLAW: first permanent disposal follows hot commissioning and precedes steady-state operation
records.finding: Hanford began hot commissioning in October 2025, permanently disposed the first vitrified low-activity-waste containers in April 2026, and reported more than 100,000 gallons vitrified by May 26, while stating that hot commissioning would continue.
